subject.title: feat: add guarded FakeCo AWS owner

question: After removing the changelog entry, should authenticated exact-head AWS lifecycle proof remain mandatory before merge, or should the FakeCo feature owner explicitly waive it?
rationale: Source inspection, contract tests, and green hosted checks cannot establish real target-account authorization or destructive lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Require live lifecycle proof
options.body: Run the exact head in the dedicated account and attach redacted plan, apply, verify, backup/restore, snapshot, and retained-data teardown artifacts.

options.title: Grant an item-specific waiver
options.body: The FakeCo feature owner explicitly accepts the remaining unobserved authorization and lifecycle risk for this exact head.

options.title: Pause for account readiness
options.body: Keep the PR open and unmerged until the protected environment and service identity are available.

recommendation.title: Require live lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Run the exact head in the dedicated account and attach redacted plan, apply, verify, backup/restore, snapshot, and retained-data teardown artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history identifies steipete as the introducer and primary owner of the FakeCo staging contract.
